title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Criminals used AI-generated deepfakes and voice cloning to impersonate trusted figures, including a real South Florida immigration attorney, to defraud people across Georgia and South Florida. The scams targeted vulnerable populations including immigrants and elderly people. This is impersonation enabled by synthetic media tools deployed with no verification that the person being contacted was actually speaking to their claimed contact.

The failure occurred at the point of initial contact, where no authentication mechanism distinguished the AI-generated voice or video from the real person. Catching this would have required the targets to verify identity through an independent channel, such as calling back a known phone number or establishing a prior secret code word. It is not established whether the deepfake tools themselves were purpose-built for fraud or whether they were general-purpose systems repurposed by criminals.

The scale suggests the tactic worked repeatedly. According to the reports, Americans reported nearly $893 million in AI-enabled scam losses in the previous year, with Florida alone reporting $39.9 million across 350 complaints. The ease of creating and distributing deepfakes meant attackers could operate at scale once they identified vulnerable targets.

summary:
# Summary

Scammers are increasingly using artificial intelligence and deepfake technology to commit fraud across Georgia and South Florida. Criminals employ AI to clone voices, create fake photos, and spoof phone numbers to impersonate trusted contacts and relatives. Notable cases include a South Florida immigration attorney whose identity was stolen to target immigrants, and a Cobb County couple who lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam. According to the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, Americans reported nearly $893 million in AI-enabled scam losses in the previous year, representing a rapidly growing trend among criminals.

The financial impact varies by state, with Florida reporting 350 AI-related complaints totaling $39.9 million in losses and Georgia reporting 71 complaints with $10.4 million in losses. Common AI-assisted scams include romance schemes, fake investment opportunities, and the grandparent scam where criminals use voice cloning to request emergency money. Authorities recommend families establish code words to verify identity, verify urgent requests through known phone numbers, and avoid sending money based on phone calls alone. The FBI warns that as AI tools become cheaper and more accessible, these scams will likely continue evolving.
